description: Set up the development groundwork without touching the live forms or sheet (an offline check suite, safeguards that block live changes without approval, project documentation, and the automatic sheet-to-form sync, kept switched off until setup) and removed an access key that had been stored in plain text. Added a searchable club dropdown to the template form so mentors pick their club instead of typing its exact spelling, with the sync keeping the list up to date. Ran an independent review of the new work, which confirmed one needed correction to the setup steps, and after an interruption resumed checking its remaining findings.

Finished the code cleanup and the fixes found in review, assigned regions to the new clubs that were missing one, and transferred the new clubs to the Jotform attendance forms. Guided the setup of the automatic sheet-to-form sync, fixed the problems that kept it from running and confirmed it works end to end, then audited the sheet and every form to confirm each new club landed correctly. Planned and drafted a required region picker for the Google Form used to register new clubs.

Completed and reviewed the required region picker on the Club Roster Form so new partners choose their region (not yet live). Started a review of all open work items and overall system health, changing nothing live, to plan the upcoming mass form update.
Finished the review of open work and delivered a roadmap covering where the system stands, every open work item and audit finding, the decisions that need leadership approval, and effort estimates.

Checked that roster submissions were flowing correctly into the enrollment sheet, then rolled out the searchable club dropdown to all attendance forms with leadership's new wording and translations (including Odia, with club names kept in English), and raised the photo upload limit to 10 MB with iPhone photos (HEIC) accepted. Delivered five new clubs and nine roster updates that had been waiting as part of the rollout, and switched automatic roster syncing to live so future changes reach the forms on their own. Resolved one club's duplicate roster so its form shows only the original girls, and confirmed that a delayed new club now appears on its regional form.

Ran a full health check of the automatic roster syncing, every attendance form and the code, and confirmed everything was green, including the first fully unattended live sync. Explained the staff notification setting and the review queue and checked recent submissions to the pre-launch forms. Once the staff inbox was set, confirmed the one step still needed before mentors' problem reports reach staff.

Corrected a mis-entered club name for an Asia partner club on the master enrollment sheet, the Asia attendance form and the template form. The club kept its code, records and roster, and the result was checked afterwards. Also built a reusable tool so future club renames can be done the same safe way.

Added Hindi and Persian translations, with their flags, to the Asia attendance form. Built an Odia flag for the language menu on every form, since Jotform has none, and fixed a display problem so it appears on the live pages. Checked the Urdu and Arabic translations already on the Asia form and filled the one gap found.

Prepared the new Global Catalyst logo at the right size for the attendance-form headers. Investigated the broken language menus on the Africa, Asia and Latin America forms and traced them to a script error in Jotform's page code. Built a correction, not yet applied, so Fundación Kaleidos can see Club Glow Traslasierra when adding girls.

Confirmed the language menus work again on all attendance forms; the outage was a temporary Jotform bug and no form changes were needed. Took the club-move correction through two rounds of review, adding safety checks and tests; nothing was changed live.

Prepared a fix for the Swahili Submit button on the attendance forms (not yet live). Finalized the club-move correction and set out the steps to apply it. Began reviewing the 11 submitted problem reports and confirmed the automatic roster sync was working correctly.

Completed the review of all 11 open problem reports: none were fixed by recent work, and one club's earlier roster fix had been undone. Built, tested and reviewed a fix so the "Process any missed form responses" menu previews and asks before running, and never re-applies old submissions, even after a time-zone change (not yet live).

Put live the fix that stops old roster submissions being re-applied, and restored the Radiant Girls roster fix on the Africa form. Added Swahili "Submit" to all forms and moved Club Glow Traslasierra to Fundación Kaleidos. Routed roster-change problem reports to the review queue and Monday e-mail; started on the remaining reports and this work log.

Tested the new read-only Salesforce connection and found that no attendance from the forms has reached Salesforce since March: the integration's Salesforce login belonged to a staff account that was deactivated in September, and it had stopped sending even before that. Investigated what Salesforce does with each submission and laid out the steps, decisions and clean-up needed to get attendance flowing again, including the submissions missed since 1 September. Fixed the work log so hours are counted on the local clock of the day the work was done, corrected the September hours, and made the dates the tools write into the enrollment sheet follow the sheet's own time zone.

Put live on all attendance forms: every club roster now sits above the Submit button, a mentor can no longer submit for more than one club at a time, and the seven clubs that share a name with another partner's club each have their own entry in the club list (club and partner together), matching their Salesforce record; also retired two duplicate clubs, fixed one Africa club whose roster could not appear, and deployed a check that stops a new club taking a name already in use. Created every active club in Salesforce - 354 new club records and 8 existing ones - each named exactly as its attendance form sends it and linked to its partner organisation, with every record read back and checked after it was written. Restored the Jotform-to-Salesforce connection on all five forms (the first attendance arrived automatically), traced the automatic security freeze that then interrupted it, built and tested the tool that will bring September's attendance into Salesforce, and drafted the new electronic-attendance checkbox for the partners' Monthly Report.

Changed a Salesforce duplicate-contact setting that made attendance records fail when two girls in a club have similar names, and checked it with test records that were then removed. Prepared the transfer of September's attendance into Salesforce (347 club sessions ready and checked, held until the form fix is live), and planned the form fix that requires at least one girl to be ticked and keeps the girls' names list correct. At the CEO's request, removed all group photos from Salesforce (27 files) while keeping the attendance records.

Brought September's attendance from the Jotform forms into Salesforce once the new form check (at least one girl ticked) was live: 355 club sessions, 4,515 attendance records and 1,969 girls, each record checked after it was written. Confirmed the new Monthly Report checkbox is live, and built the test report "Jotform Monthly Attendance (test)" (September: 4,712 attendance records, 24 partners, 147 clubs). Looked into a partner's report that the Asia attendance form would not load their clubs: the form works for all eight of its clubs in every language, and an old copy of the Asia form that is still switched on is the likely cause. Turned the attendance report into a Salesforce dashboard for leadership: girls who attended last month and this month, club sessions and clubs reporting by week and month, attendance by partner and by curriculum module, and the clubs that have not sent attendance, with a partner filter; every figure was checked against the underlying records, and two problems found that way were corrected.

Finished the Salesforce attendance dashboard: prepared, checked and confirmed live the corrections to the "this month" figure and to the list of clubs with no attendance, added a short guide on the dashboard, and wrote the operating notes. Linked two new clubs to their partner in Salesforce and planned how new clubs' Salesforce records will be created automatically. Fixed a small fault in the work log tool. Reviewed four new requests against the live forms and Salesforce (the module choice on the attendance form; a report of clubs that did not submit or sent an empty submission; the cost of sending the group photos to Google Drive; attendance totals that include the three partners who report counts instead of using the form), and wrote and agreed the plans for them.

Built the automatic creation of Salesforce records for new clubs: when a new club is added to an attendance form, its Salesforce club record is created first, under the right partner, with checks that prevent duplicates; it stays switched off until the Salesforce access is set up. Reviewed and tested it, and confirmed against the live data that every current club already has the right record. Built the agreed changes offline: storage and module-shape checks in the form audit, two Salesforce correction tools, the Salesforce fields and processor change prepared for deployment, the new report definitions, and the sheet marker that takes non-Jotform partners' clubs off the forms together with tools to deactivate clubs and pause a form; all reviewed, nothing live changed yet. In the afternoon, merged the duplicate girl records in Salesforce so each girl has one record, and released the attendance processor change that ignores stray spacing in names, so new submissions no longer create duplicates.

Checked the Salesforce attendance reports end to end: every number on the dashboard and reports matches the underlying records, and every attendance form submission since 1 September is accounted for in Salesforce. Linked two new clubs to their partner organization and flagged one submission with a mistyped session date for follow-up. Opened the attendance dashboard and reports to all staff users, with the access they need to see the details.
Updated the Group Photo field on all the attendance forms so its instruction asks for one photo of everyone in attendance, in every form language, and checked each form afterwards.

Designed, built and released a Special Events option on all the attendance forms, starting with Welcome Sessions, so clubs can record one-off sessions alongside the curriculum; it was reviewed, tested and checked on every form before the automatic sync was switched back on. Confirmed the photo upload limit (10 MB, one photo) on every form, and brought the work log up to date.
